chapters.html:
"Snowy, De! What brings you two to the Garden of Life?"

Tribbie waves them over from where she sits on the grass with Trinnon and Trianne, soft-petaled flowers between their fingers.

"Lady Tribbie!" Phainon greets her brightly, waving back. "Lady Trinnon, Lady Trianne! Me and Mydei were on our way to the market."

"De going to the market on a weekend? That's rare," Trianne snickers. "What do you need so urgently you're willing to go through that?"

There is silence. Phainon turns towards Mydei, confused. Mydei ignored his greetings earlier today, but he just assumed he was grumpy about something and didn't pry. Though, usually Mydei huffed or gave some sort of verbal confirmation that he heard Phainon rather than pure silence, but Phainon didn't really chalk it up to anything much. Now though? Something was seriously wrong if Mydei was refusing to speak to Lady Trianne.

"Uh, De? Are you okay?"

Now that Phainon is looking at Mydei, he sees a look on his face he doesn't remember often seeing. A look of conflict, as if torn between two emotions. His mouth opens, closes, and his eyes narrow, grinding his teeth before attempting to speak again, no sound coming out. His eyes dart all over the garden, from the triplets of fate to the chimeras rolling around to the benches.

"Are you looking for something?" Phainon offers.

Mydei looks at him, with something heavy and scrutinising in his gaze, surveying him. It feels similar to the look Mydei gave him when they first met, outside Okhema's gates with the Kremnoan detachment. It's slightly different that instead of appraising, Mydei's gaze almost seems pleading, like he's looking for something that he wants to be there.

Mydei's gaze flicks to the triplets again, then back to Phainon, then he looks back to the triplets and opens his mouth, then closes it, then back to Phainon, and this indecisiveness is clearly troubling triplets, concerning mounting on their faces.

Trinnon speaks first. "De, it's okay if you can't speak."

"Yeah, De!" Tribbie pipes up. "Don't force yourself. We'll chat later, okay!"

Mydei frowns. He tries to speak again, but Phainon takes his hand. "Mydei," he murmurs, "let's get going, okay?" He squeezes his hand. "I'm sure Lady Tribbie, Trianne and Trinnon are all very busy with their current flowery endevaours."

"Totally!" Trianne cheers. "Come back later, and you can tell us everything you wanted to say, and we'll tell you what we're doing too!"

Trinnon presses a red flower into Mydei's gauntled palm. "We're not upset. Take your time."

Mydei finally looks somewhat assured, nodding his head, tucking the little flower into his sash.

"Let's go then, Mydei?" Phainon tugs on their still-linked hands.

Mydei turns to him, face carefully blank, and nods, dragging them both to the exit.

//

“Lord Phainon, Lord Mydei.”

Phainon whirls around at the soft voice. “Castorice! What are you doing here?”

They’re not far from Marmoreal Market. Far enough that there aren’t many people, close enough to still see some stalls.

Castorice makes a slightly guilty expression. “I was making my way to the baths when I saw something I’d like to buy… I’d like to go over and buy it, but…”

Right. It was the weekend after all, the streets were more crowded than usual.

Castorice turns to look at Mydei. “Is something wrong, Lord Mydei?”

Phainon turns to him too, just to see that same agitated facial expression before.

He raises a gauntlet hand and makes a come here gesture with his hand, causing all three of their eyes to widen. Mydei’s never once beckoned anyone like that.

Not to mention, Castorice really couldn’t move closer, what with Phainon right there. Mydei is more than aware of that. Frustration mounts in Mydei’s gaze, and Castorice looks on in concern.

“Lord Mydei -“

Mydei grabs Phainon arm and pulls him towards himself. Phainon freezes, completely helpless. He feels Mydei's warm breath against his ear.

"We’ll get it,” he whispers, voice hoarse but soft round the edges. He releases Phainon just as suddenly as he yanked him.

Phainon stares at him with wide eyes. All Mydei does is gesture to Castorice.

“Oh uh - he said we’ll get it.”

“Are you sure? It’s really no hassle on my part, I didn’t really have anything to do today.” Castorice’s eyes flick between the two of them, almost unsure of who to address.

Phainon doesn’t need to look at Mydei to know what he’s going to say. “It’s really no bother. We’re on our way there ourselves.”

“If you’re sure then…. Thank you both.”

Castorice stands there, almost biting her lip. “Uh, Lord Phainon, a word please, if you don’t mind.”

“Of course.” He looks over to Mydei who nods.

Castorice walks over to a slightly more private corner, and Phainon follows.

“Is there something troubling you, Cas?”

Castorice smooths her dress down and holds her hands. “Did I do something to upset Lord Mydei?”

“Upset - No, no you didn’t. Mydei can’t speak to anyone today, he was like that with Lady Tribios too.”

Castorice breathed a sigh of relief. “I see… that is a relief. I was worried I did something to displease him, what with the way he was looking. Is Lord Mydei okay then?”

It’s Phainon’s turn to sigh, though for entirely different reasons. “I don’t know. He wasn’t talking from when I met him earlier. I was planning on just going to the market with him as planned, but maybe I should have made write down what’s wrong with him, huh?”

“I think going to the market is the right choice. If Lord Mydei didn’t want to, then he would have said. Continue what you have planned, and then talk to him. It might put him at ease; you know he’d hate to disrupt already made plans.”

Phainon smiles. “As comforting as ever Castorice, thank you. Pick a place to sit in the plaza, and me and Mydei will find you once we’re done.”

Castorice returns his smile with her own small one. “Of course. I’m glad to have helped.”

—

Phainon returns to Mydei’s side, tapping his shoulder.

Mydei turns to him, golden eyes clear and face calm. He doesn’t look upset, unlike when they were in the garden and something was clearly eating at him.

“We’re good to head off, Mydei.”

Mydei nods, and they walk off together.

//

Phainon means to find out what’s wrong with Mydei, really, but every time he broaches it Mydei shakes his head and waves him off. Even when they finish shopping and arrive back at the heir’s living quarters and paper is readily available, Mydei refuses to elaborate. Phainon doesn’t feel comfortable pushing him to open up if he’s not ready, but even more if Mydei seems so openly okay. He’s not faking it, smiling when they pass some Kremnoans in the market and waving without a trace of forcing himself.

When Phainon told Mydei about Castorice’s worry, once they finished their shopping Mydei pressed the sunset fabric Castorice wanted into her hands and squeezed them reassuringly between his own, smiling softly. He didn’t need to speak for his sentiment to be understood.

They end up in the kitchens, Phainon watching forlornly as Mydei prepares dinner for everyone.

Perhaps Mydei really was fine and decided he just didn’t want to speak today. That was fine too. It still didn’t feel right though. Phainon sighed, not that Mydei could hear it over the sound of his chopping and the bubbling of the nearby pot.

The sound of heels resonated through the hallway, and Phainon sat up a little straighter and the movement of Mydei’s hand stilled.

“Lady Aglaea,” he greeted.

“Phainon,” she says, inclining her head. “And Mydei.”

Mydei wipes his down on his apron and walks over to them. He nods at Lady Aglaea before leaning down to whisper to Phainon.

“Good afternoon.”

Phainon’s been through this enough today to know Mydei isn’t talking to him.

“He said good afternoon, Lady Aglaea.”

Aglaea hums. “The triplets informed me. You have trouble speaking today, Mydei?”

Another nod from Mydei.

“I hope it doesn’t impede you too much. Since you can speak to Phainon, I’m assuming it’s not something physically wrong?”

A shake of the head.

“Good. If it continues for a prolonged period of time, then please see Hyacine.”

Another low whisper in his ear, golden locks shifting so loudly against the shell of his ear. “Not long. Gone by tonight.”

Aglaea looks at Phainon expectantly. “… he said he’ll be fine by tonight.”

“Very well. May I have a moment, Phainon?”

Mydei, having been effectively dismissed, goes back cooking. Aglaea gracefully takes a seat beside him, but it doesn’t make Phainon feel any less like he’s a child about to get chastised.

“Are you okay, Phainon?”

Phainon blinks. Mydei’s the one not speaking. Why is she concerned about him?

“Uh, yeah. Why?”

“Mydei is troubling you.”

Phainon’s eyes flick to the side. “He’s right there, Lady Aglaea.”

“And he can’t hear. So?”

Phainon sighs, slumping in his chair, hand threading through his hair. “I don’t know… it’s not really a problem…”

“Phainon.”

“Okay okay.” Phainon folds immediately. “I’m aware this is a stupid way to feel, by the way, but the whole day, Mydei’s been using me to talk to other people. And I’m glad! That he feels comfortable and trusts me enough to relay his words. But when it’s just us, he’s entirely silent. I don’t know… I just feel kinda strange that he doesn’t mind talking to others but not me.”

“Again, I know that it’s stupid to feel this way -“

“Phainon.”

Phainon shuts up.

“I can’t speak for Mydei, but this is my interpretation of what may be going through his head. Who were the people he used you to talk to?”

“Uhh, the Kremnoans, Cas, you, the sellers at the market, and a few others.”

Aglaea hums. The scent of lemon trails through the air.

“What did he tell you to say?”

“Well for you, it was a greeting. For Cas, it was to tell her we’d get something. With all the vendors, it was when he needed something they didn’t have on display.”

“So, he was only speaking out of necessity, correct? So that means, with you, he did not feel it was necessary to speak. Think about what that might mean, hmm?”

She stands elegantly. “That soup smells wonderful, Mydei. I will see you when it is served.”

Mydei nods, giving her a brief wave. Lady Aglaea moves past Phainon, giving him a meaningful look as she pats his shoulder.

“And my final and most important piece of wisdom - talk to him.”

And away she glides.

//

They settle in Phainon’s room after they’ve eaten, Mydei lying back on his kline.

“Mydei?”

Mydei hums.

“Is there a reason why you could speak to everyone else today but not me? I mean - yes me because you were talking through me - but not to me - “

Mydei holds a hand up for silence, and then gestures for Phainon to come close.

Phainon takes a seat beside him as Mydei sits up. Mydei doesn’t take hold him, but rather presses his shoulder against Phainon’s back so he can easily whisper to him.

Phainon can feel him breathing, tickling his hairs and ghosting over his cheek.

“You. Comfortable, with you. No - “

A long breath. “ - not needed talking.”

Mydei places a hand on his cheek to turn Phainon to face him. His eyes gaze into his. Do you understand?

So, he didn’t speak to Phainon not because he thought he was unworthy, but -

“Does speaking trouble you, Mydei? I mean - I know it must - and agh, I’m just asking you to talk all over again - “

Mydei smiles indulgently. “Can’t talk,” he whispers. “Hard.”

“So you didn’t speak to me because it made you comfortable?”

A nod.

Phainon smiles brightly, the tension leaking from his body. He feels giddy, eyes curved into crescents. Mydei trusted him to convey his words. Mydei felt comfortable to not force himself to speak around him, didn’t keep up the same appearance he did everyone else.

“I can hear your ego, Deliverer.”

Phainon blinks. A full sentence.

“Are you better now, Mydei?”

“Yes,” Mydei says fondly. “Thank you for looking after me, rough as I was. After a point, I was silent simply because I was comfortable that way, and not because I couldn’t.”

Phainon blinks again. “So something was wrong!”

“I had a conversation with Krateros shortly before I met up with you,” Mydei confides. “It… was not a pleasant one, and my voice clammed up. But by the time you asked me, I truly was alright. I just liked the feeling of not speaking. Sorry if I troubled you.” Mydei pauses, rolling something in his head. “I should apologise to everyone else too. I don’t know what I was thinking -“

“Don’t!”

Mydei’s eyes are wide, and Phainon winces. He didn’t mean to interrupt. “I mean, I won’t lie you worried a few people, but I think all of us can agree it was fine. If it makes you comfortable, what’s wrong with being silent? The Kremnoan’s didn’t seem surprised - are they used to it?”

Mydei nods. “I had a lot of silent days with them. They’re aware of how I can get.”

“See! It’s totally fine, and not a bother to anyone, so don’t think you need to go and apologise, okay?”

Mydei makes a face. “At least Castorice, gesturing to her was rude.”

“It wasn’t rude, Mydei.” Phainon smiles, half exasperated. “You wanted her to come close so you could whisper to her too, right? You did that because you wanted to talk to her. I’m sure she wasn’t even offended in the first place. But sure, you can explain it to her.”

Mydei scoffs. “So the great Deliverer can parse my intentions towards anyone but himself, huh?”

“Hey!” Phainon pulls away mock-wounded. It’s different when it’s himself. “How can you talk right now anyway?”

Mydei shrugs. “You were happy. The urge to talk overcame the want to be silent.” He shoves his shoulder. “Don’t get all blushy now, Deliverer!”

Phainon giggles. Every warm and harsh word, every soft and awkward whisper, he’ll keep them safe.
